Scope props shared by framework providers.

## Properties

### enabled?

```ts
optional enabled?: boolean;
```

Defined in: [adapter.ts:435](https://github.com/TanStack/hotkeys/blob/main/packages/hotkeys/src/adapter.ts#L435)

Set false to deactivate this provider's scope, and the scopes of
providers nested in it, without unmounting. Defaults to true.

***

### exclusive?

```ts
optional exclusive?: 
  | boolean
  | {
  allow: readonly string[];
};
```

Defined in: [adapter.ts:430](https://github.com/TanStack/hotkeys/blob/main/packages/hotkeys/src/adapter.ts#L430)

While mounted and enabled, suspend hotkeys in every other scope,
including `'global'`, except scopes of nested providers. Pass
`{ allow: [...] }` to keep other scopes active, such as `'global'`. Use
with `scope`, for dialogs and other overlays.

***

### scope?

```ts
optional scope?: string;
```

Defined in: [adapter.ts:423](https://github.com/TanStack/hotkeys/blob/main/packages/hotkeys/src/adapter.ts#L423)

Scope for hotkeys registered inside this provider, active while it is
mounted and enabled. Defaults to the parent provider's scope, or
`'global'` at the root. App hotkeys that declare a scope keep it.

***

### suspendCharacterKeys?

```ts
optional suspendCharacterKeys?: boolean;
```

Defined in: [adapter.ts:449](https://github.com/TanStack/hotkeys/blob/main/packages/hotkeys/src/adapter.ts#L449)

While mounted, suspend document-level character key shortcuts across the
app, including hotkeys such as `K`, `?`, `Shift+K`, `Space`, or
`['G', 'H']` that use only keys that type a character. Wire this option to
a user setting so people who use speech input or press keys by accident
can turn single-key shortcuts off for WCAG 2.1.4 (Character Key
Shortcuts). Hotkeys with `Control`, `Alt`, or `Meta`, non-character keys
such as `Escape` or `F1`, and hotkeys targeted at an element other than
the body keep working. This option applies even when the provider sets
`enabled` to `false`, and to every hotkey in the app, not only those under
the provider. See
`HotkeyManager.suspendCharacterKeys`. Defaults to `false`.
